audit_findings.title: Contingent acquisition consideration is missing from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $80.716 million filed fair value at 2025-12-31, equal to $2.55 per diluted share; H1 2026 remeasurement loss was $25.570 million and a $38.470 million Infocenter payment followed on 2026-07-13, but the exact 2026-06-30 liability is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds cash to equity value but does not subtract earnout claims, while OE excludes or reverses their remeasurement expense and does not include settlement cash outflows.
audit_findings.evidence: The total purchase price also includes the estimated fair value of earn out payments of approximately $ 37,790,000 , which provide an incentive opportunity for the sellers to earn up to $ 66,000,000 , contingent upon Inspire11 achieving certain EBITDA performance targets through September 2027.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated bridge omission, not merely a contingent business risk. Filed earnout liabilities relate to businesses already contributing earnings, and their recorded value alone equals 1.7% of the $4.860 billion base equity value. Maximum contractual payouts are materially higher, so the omission can affect scenario values and the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June 30 fair-value liability and remaining maximum payout for SADA, Amdaris, Infocenter, Inspire11 and Sekuro; deduct the settlement-date present value not already captured in OE and rerun every scenario and the buy-below value.

audit_findings.title: Projected growth may require unmodeled working-capital financing
audit_findings.magnitude: $154.308 million computed H1 2026 increase in accounts receivable plus inventories less accounts payable; operating cash flow was $20.140 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Incremental receivables and inventory reduce distributable OE; debt-funded working capital instead increases future interest expense retained in equity-level OE.
audit_findings.evidence: This generally means in periods of growing hardware sales, we typically use cash from operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The operating requirement is demonstrated, but omission from the forecast is not established because the supplied valuation does not show how its 28.7% RONTA or reinvestment calculation treats working capital. The computed H1 movement is large relative to $302.8 million anchor OE, but agent-transaction netting, payment timing and vendor mix make it unsuitable as a normalized requirement without further analysis.
audit_findings.action: Expose the scenario reinvestment formula, calculate normalized incremental operating working capital per dollar of organic sales or gross profit excluding agent-flow distortions, and rerun the growth cases with either that cash investment or the corresponding financing cost.

audit_findings.title: The FY2025 earnings numerator may contain a stale interest burden
audit_findings.magnitude: $12.790 million computed annualized pre-tax gap between Q2 2026 net interest expense of $24.409 million and FY2025 net interest expense of $84.846 million; approximately $9.337 million after the filed 27.0% Q2 tax rate
audit_findings.mechanism: Because debt principal is not deducted from the bridge, the current cost of the ABL, fixed-rate notes and inventory financing must be reflected in the OE anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: During 2025, weighted average borrowings under our ABL facility were $ 754,706,000 .
audit_findings.explanation: The mismatch is demonstrated: June 2026 debt was $1.475 billion and the filing attributes higher 2026 interest expense to higher borrowing balances. If the computed gap persisted, it would reduce anchor OE by about 3.1%. Materiality remains unresolved because quarter-end debt, quarterly interest income, seasonal borrowing and lower ABL rates do not establish a normalized full-year burden.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile average Q2 borrowings and interest by facility, including imputed inventory-financing interest and interest income; normalize after-tax OE at the current capital structure and rerun the valuation.

audit_findings.title: All cash was treated as surplus despite operating and repatriation constraints
audit_findings.magnitude: $316.4 million of the $363.482 million June 2026 cash balance was held by foreign subsidiaries, or 87.0% of cash and $9.99 per diluted share; the full cash addition equals $11.47 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: The equity bridge adds cash dollar-for-dollar, although minimum operating cash and repatriation leakage should remain within the operating business or be deducted from distributable cash.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, we had approximately $ 306.6 million in cash and cash equivalents in certain of our foreign subsidiaries, primarily residing in Canada, Australia, the Netherlands and New Zealand.
audit_findings.explanation: Treating every dollar as surplus is a demonstrated modeling assumption, but the record does not demonstrate that all foreign cash is trapped: the company can remit some through intercompany settlements or dividends. Nevertheless, the exposed amount equals 6.5% of base equity value and exceeds the $7.60 per-share gap between market price and base value, so a reasonable non-surplus portion could change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain June cash by jurisdiction and legal entity, intercompany payable capacity, withholding and other repatriation costs, restrictions, and a normalized minimum operating-cash requirement; rerun the bridge using only excess distributable cash.

audit_findings.title: Historical OE depends on unstable partner funding
audit_findings.magnitude: $113.371 million of partner funding reduced 2025 selling and administrative expenses, down $13.688 million from 2024; partner funding recorded in cost of goods sold and services revenue is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Reduced rebates, marketing reimbursements, referral fees or cloud incentives lower gross profit and OE and may invalidate the assumed growth and margin path.
audit_findings.evidence: We regularly experience partner funding program changes that reduce the incentives many partners make available to us and that change the requirements for earning such incentives.
audit_findings.explanation: Partner funding is significant and actual cloud-program changes already affected 2025, but those effects are present in the $302.8 million FY2025 anchor. The finding concerns additional future program deterioration, for which the record supplies no announced amount or probability. It should therefore be monitored rather than booked as a current correction.
audit_findings.action: Track quarterly partner funding by accounting line and major vendor, compare its 2026 run rate with 2025, and rerun margin and growth assumptions if announced changes or sustained declines exceed what the anchor already captures.

audit_findings.title: Late-2025 acquisitions create a run-rate perimeter mismatch
audit_findings.mechanism: A partial-year acquisition contribution can understate current OE, while incremental interest, integration costs and earnout claims can offset that benefit through OE or the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Our results of operations include the results of Inspire11, Sekuro and Infocenter from their respective acquisition dates.
audit_findings.explanation: The timing mismatch is demonstrated because FY2025 contains only three months of Inspire11 and two months of Sekuro while the June 2026 balance sheet contains their financing and obligations. The filing says historical results would not have been materially affected by either acquisition, but it does not disclose acquired OE, current organic performance or a complete after-financing run rate. Direction and materiality therefore cannot be established from the record.
audit_findings.action: Compute trailing-twelve-month OE through June 2026 on a consistent perimeter, separately identifying acquired operating earnings, organic changes, integration costs, incremental after-tax interest and earnout claims; then rerun the anchor and document the perimeter ruling.
